examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: wait atomically consumes a permit or blocks; signal releases one. A binary semaphore can serialize critical updates, while a count of two permits overlapping updates and lost writes. Track which locks a blocked thread still holds. For output-pattern questions, derive forced prefixes and barriers before enumerating arbitrary schedules.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A counting semaphore begins at 3. Four processes each wait once without any intervening signal. How many can proceed past wait?

**Answer: 3.** The first three successful waits consume the three permits and reduce the count to zero. The fourth process blocks until another process signals. Exactly three can proceed.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A binary semaphore and a mutex can differ in ownership rules. Releasing a mutex from a different thread is not generally permitted.

Waiting for a resource while holding an unrelated needed lock can introduce deadlock.
